description:
Program Description

The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a one-time initiative designed to support institutions in recruiting internationally based Early Career Researchers to Canada. Emerging Leaders will receive research funding and institutional support to advance transformative research in Canada’s strategic priority areas, build partnerships across sectors and borders, and translate their research into applications and impacts that benefit Canadians and the world. The Faculty of Engineering (http://www.mcgill.ca/engineering) and the Trottier Institute for Sustainability in Engineering and Design (http://www.mcgill.ca/tised) at McGill University invites applications for a full-me tenure-track Assistant Professor position to advance transformational research programs that support the growth of Canada’s global leadership in the following strategic priority area:

  • Clean technology and resource value chains

Emerging Leaders must have an independent program of research that demonstrates strategic alignment with this priority area. The award provides $100,000 per year for six years to McGill University to support the salary costs associated with the successful Emerging Leader appointment as well as direct research expenses, with the possibility of extension for a further six years.

Successful candidates will be expected to begin a full-me tenure-track appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor no later than August 5, 2027, within the academic unit(s) most closely aligned with their expertise and research interests. The specific academic affiliation(s) will be determined as part of the recruitment process.

Job Duties

Successful candidates will have a strong commitment to the mission of the University, through excellence in research, teaching, and service.

Successful candidates will be expected to lead an independently funded research program, teach undergraduate and graduate courses, develop courses in their areas of specialization, supervise and mentor graduate students, and contribute to the intellectual life of the University.

Qualifications and Education Requirements Only candidates who were internationally based, both working and residing outside Canada, on August 5, 2026, are eligible.

Candidates must be within five years following the start date of their first research-related appointment, minus the length of any eligible delays in research. Recent graduates and postdoctoral fellows may also be eligible. Research-related appointments are defined as those where the individual has the autonomy to conduct research independently.

Eligible leaves, including maternity, parental, medical, and bereavement leave, are credited as twice the amount of me taken. Professional leaves, including training, sabbatical, and administrative leave, are not credited.

A PhD is required by McGill University for appointment to a tenure-track position; however, it is not a requirement of the Impact+ Emerging Leaders Program itself.

Candidates should review the eligibility and selection criteria for the Impact+ Program prior to applying.

Canadians living abroad who wish to relocate to Canada are encouraged to apply. In the Faculty of Engineering, registration in a Canadian professional engineering association is required within the first five years following hiring.

Application Process

Applications must be submitted through Workday, McGill’s HR management system, using the following link: https://mcgill.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/McGill_Careers/job/McConnell-Eng-Bldg/Assistant-Professor---Emerging-Leaders_JR0000079891

Use a personal email address when creating an account in Workday. Refer to the How to Apply for a Job (for External Candidates) job aid for instructions on how to apply.

Required Documents

The application package should include the documents listed below and must be merged into one single PDF file not exceeding 5 MB.

  • Cover letter
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Statement of research describing current and future research, alignment with the strategic priority area, and potential for knowledge translation, mobilization, and application of research results (maximum four pages)
  • Research infrastructure needs: laboratory space, equipment
  • Teaching statement and dossier
  • Contact information for three references

Job Details

Job Type: Tenure-track
Rank: Assistant Professor
Salary: Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Posting Period

To be considered for this position, the application package must be submitted online at the link above by the closing date of October 27, 2026.

Inquiries from potential candidates are welcome and will be treated in strict confidence. Correspondence can be directed to (subhasis.ghoshal@mcgill.ca), and Brandon Xia, Associate Dean of Research and Innova on, Faculty of Engineering (brandon.xia@mcgill.ca).

Commitment to Equity and Diversity

Please note that to work at McGill University, you must be both authorized to work in Canada and willing to work in the province of Quebec at the campus where the position is based / located. McGill University offers immigration and relocation support for selected candidates.

McGill University is an English-language university where most teaching and research activities are conducted in the English language, thereby requiring English communication both verbally and in writing.

McGill University is committed to equity and diversity within its community and values academic rigour and excellence. We welcome and encourage applications from racialized persons/visible minorities, women, Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, ethnic minorities, and persons of minority sexual orientations and gender identities, as well as from all qualified candidates with the skills and knowledge to engage productively with diverse communities.

At McGill, research that reflects diverse intellectual traditions, methodologies, and modes of dissemination and translation is valued and encouraged. Candidates are invited to demonstrate their research impact both within and across academic disciplines and in other sectors, such as government, communities, or industry.

McGill further recognizes and fairly considers the impact of leaves (e.g., family care or health-related) that may contribute to career interruptions or slowdowns. Candidates are encouraged to signal any leave that affected productivity, or that may have had an effect on their career path. This information will be considered to ensure the equitable assessment of the candidate’s record.

McGill implements an employment equity program and encourages members of designated equity groups to self-identify. It further seeks to ensure the equitable treatment and full inclusion of persons with disabilities by striving for the implementation of universal design principles transversally, across all facets of the University community, and through accommodation policies and procedures. Persons with disabilities who anticipate needing accommodations for any part of the application process may contact, in confidence, Catherine Roy accessibilityrequest.hr@mcgill.ca.

description:
About Desert Research Institute
The Desert Research Institute (DRI) is Nevada's non-profit environmental research institution and a world-renowned leader in the advancement of scientific knowledge related to the Earth's atmosphere, water resources, ecosystems, and environmental systems. Founded in 1959, DRI was established with a singular purpose: to apply scientific discovery and innovation to solve complex environmental challenges and improve lives in Nevada and around the world. Today, DRI's researchers conduct groundbreaking work on every continent, addressing some of society's most pressing issues, including climate change, water sustainability, environmental health, extreme events, renewable energy, ecosystem resilience, and emerging environmental threats.

Headquartered across major research campuses in Reno and Las Vegas, DRI comprises more than 600 scientists, engineers, students, and professional staff and supports approximately 175 principal investigators spanning more than 40 scientific disciplines. The Institute generates sponsored research activity through a diversified portfolio of federal, state, local, foundation, and private-sector partnerships. DRI's researchers are recognized internationally for translating scientific inquiry into practical solutions that inform policy, strengthen communities, and address challenges affecting human and environmental well-being.

A Distinctive Role in Higher Education
DRI occupies a unique position within the American research landscape. As one of the institutions comprising the Nevada System of Higher Education (NSHE), DRI shares the public-service mission and academic values of a major higher education system while operating with a research-centric focus uncommon among traditional universities. Unlike most academic institutions, DRI's faculty are not burdened by significant teaching responsibilities and instead devote their efforts to pursuing high-impact research, securing external funding, advancing innovation, and collaborating across disciplines and organizations around the world. This distinctive model creates an environment that combines the intellectual rigor of academia with the entrepreneurial spirit and agility often associated with leading research institutes and national laboratories.

DRI's relationship with NSHE is both unique and strategically important. As Nevada's dedicated research institution, DRI collaborates extensively with Nevada's colleges and universities through joint research initiatives, faculty partnerships, workforce development efforts, graduate student engagement, and scientific training opportunities. In doing so, DRI serves as a critical bridge between discovery, education, innovation, and public impact, helping to strengthen Nevada's research ecosystem while advancing scientific solutions that benefit the state, the nation, and the broader global community.

Science That Matters Now®
DRI is guided by the belief that science should not exist solely for academic advancement but should create meaningful impact in the real world. The Institute's "Science That Matters Now®" philosophy reflects a commitment to delivering timely, actionable research that helps communities, governments, industries, and decision-makers navigate an increasingly complex environmental landscape. Whether advancing water security in arid regions, developing solutions to improve air quality, supporting climate resilience initiatives, or informing public policy through objective scientific expertise, DRI's work is characterized by relevance, rigor, and impact.

The Institute's culture is equally distinctive. DRI attracts highly entrepreneurial scientists who operate in a competitive, externally funded research environment that rewards innovation, collaboration, and scientific excellence. Researchers are encouraged to pursue bold ideas, transcend traditional disciplinary boundaries, and engage with partners across government, industry, academia, and the nonprofit sector.

The Leadership Moment
DRI enters its next chapter from a position of considerable strength. As climate variability, water scarcity, environmental health concerns, energy transitions, and natural resource challenges increasingly shape public policy and economic development, the demand for credible scientific research has never been greater. At the same time, the research funding landscape continues to evolve, creating new opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, technology translation, public-private partnerships, and expanded engagement with government and industry stakeholders.

Against this backdrop, the Vice President for Research will play a transformative role in shaping DRI's future. As the Institute's chief research strategist and second-ranking executive, this leader will help define scientific priorities, strengthen DRI's national and international profile, foster innovation across the research enterprise, expand strategic partnerships, and position the Institute to capitalize on emerging opportunities. Working closely with the President, research leadership, faculty scientists, policymakers, and external partners, the Vice President for Research will help ensure that DRI remains at the forefront of environmental discovery while amplifying its impact on Nevada, the nation, and the world. The next Vice President for Research will inherit a strong and respected research enterprise while helping shape its next phase of growth, visibility, and influence in an increasingly competitive and rapidly evolving research environment.

The Opportunity

Position: Vice President for Research
Location: Las Vegas or Reno, NV
Reporting Relationship: President
Website: https://dri.edu/

The Role of the Vice President for Research
The Desert Research Institute seeks an accomplished, entrepreneurial, and externally focused scientific leader to serve as its next Vice President for Research (VPR). Reporting directly to the President and serving as the Institute's second-ranking executive, the VPR will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of one of the nation's premier environmental research organizations. This is an exceptional opportunity to help lead a globally respected institution that combines scientific excellence, public impact, and entrepreneurial innovation in service to Nevada, the nation, and the world. DRI is Nevada's dedicated research institution within the Nevada System of Higher Education and occupies a distinctive position at the intersection of academic research, public service, government partnership, and applied scientific discovery.

As DRI's chief research officer and principal scientific strategist, the Vice President for Research will oversee a research enterprise comprising approximately 175 faculty scientists spanning more than 40 scientific disciplines, three research divisions and a research portfolio generating more than $50 million annually in sponsored research activity. The VPR will directly lead a team of senior research and administrative leaders while helping drive the strategic growth, impact, and long-term sustainability of a research portfolio supported by federal agencies, state and local governments, private industry, foundations, and other partners. Working across a highly entrepreneurial, externally funded environment, this leader will help identify emerging scientific opportunities, foster interdisciplinary collaboration. They will also position DRI for continued growth and influence within an increasingly competitive research landscape that is facing complex, dynamic challenges from external environments.

Importantly, this role extends well beyond the administration of research programs. DRI seeks a visible and influential scientific ambassador who will represent the Institute among policymakers, funding agencies, scientific organizations, industry leaders, and strategic partners locally, nationally, and internationally. The Vice President for Research will cultivate relationships that expand research opportunities, strengthen DRI's reputation, and enhance the Institute's ability to address complex environmental challenges. Working closely with local, state and federal agencies, Nevada's congressional delegation, state and local leaders, industry and nonprofit partners, and collaborators throughout higher education, this executive will serve as a compelling advocate for scientific innovation, research investment, and evidence-based solutions that improve lives and inform policy.

The Vice President for Research will also serve as a key strategic partner to the President and executive leadership team in shaping the Institute's future direction. This leader will demonstrate foresight, mentorship and empathy in working collaboratively with research division directors and administrative leaders across advancement, finance, communications, human resources, facilities, legal affairs, information technology, and other key functions to ensure alignment between DRI's research priorities and broader institutional objectives. The successful candidate will combine vision with execution, strengthening the systems, talent, partnerships, and infrastructure necessary to support scientific excellence while advancing DRI's position as a globally recognized leader in environmental research and innovation.

This is a rare opportunity to influence not only the future of a distinguished research institution, but also the trajectory of scientific discovery in areas critical to society's future. At a time when there is unprecedented uncertainty and pressure due to many external factors, communities, governments, and industries increasingly depend on trusted science to address challenges involving climate, water, environmental health, resilience, and sustainability, the Vice President for Research will have the opportunity to shape research agendas, elevate scientific impact, and advance an institution whose work truly embodies its guiding principle: Science That Matters Now®.

Key Responsibilities
The Vice President for Research serves as the chief architect of DRI's research strategy and the principal leader of one of the nation's most distinctive environmental research enterprises. In partnership with the President, research leadership, faculty scientists, and external stakeholders, the Vice President for Research will advance scientific excellence, expand research capacity, accelerate growth and increase impact, cultivate strategic partnerships, and strengthen DRI's position as a globally respected leader in environmental science and innovation. This executive will help shape the future trajectory of the Institute by fostering scientific collaboration, championing faculty success, identifying emerging opportunities, and representing DRI among funding agencies, policymakers, industry leaders, and research partners across the United States and internationally. Balancing institutional leadership with external engagement, the Vice President for Research will help ensure DRI remains a destination for world-class scientists, a trusted source of scientific expertise, and an organization whose research continues to improve lives and inform solutions to critical environmental challenges.

Strategic Research Leadership and Enterprise Growth

  • Develop and advance a compelling vision for DRI's research enterprise that aligns with the Institute's mission, strategic priorities, and long-term aspirations.
  • Lead institution-wide research planning efforts, identifying emerging scientific opportunities, areas of competitive advantage, and pathways for growth.
  • Strengthen and expand DRI's portfolio of federally funded state-funded, industry-sponsored, and philanthropic research initiatives.
  • Foster interdisciplinary collaboration across DRI's research divisions and encourage innovative approaches to complex scientific challenges.
  • Ensure the Institute remains positioned as a leader in environmental science, natural resource management, climate resilience, environmental health, and related fields.

External Engagement, Partnerships, and Research Advancement

  • Serve as a chief ambassador for DRI within the scientific community and among key external stakeholders locally, nationally, and internationally.
  • Cultivate and strengthen relationships with federal, state, and local agencies, congressional, state, and local elected representatives, industry leaders, foundations and other nonprofits, national laboratories, research universities, and strategic partners.
  • Identify and pursue new opportunities for research funding, strategic alliances, and collaborative initiatives that advance DRI's mission and institutional priorities.
  • Enhance DRI's visibility and reputation through participation in scientific, governmental, industry, and community forums.
  • Advocate for the value and impact of DRI's research, performance and position as the Institute that is rising to and embracing new technologies, artificial intelligence, a changing global economy and tougher competitive dynamics.

Faculty Excellence, Talent Development, and Research Culture

  • Foster an environment that enables faculty, researchers, and research staff to achieve the highest levels of scientific excellence and impact.
  • Recruit, retain, develop, and support outstanding scientists who contribute to DRI's success and future growth.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor and resource to faculty across all career stages, helping them navigate opportunities, challenges, and professional development.
  • Encourage mentorship, leadership development, collaboration, and knowledge-sharing across the research enterprise.
  • Oversee faculty promotion processes, institutional research awards, and programs designed to support research excellence and career advancement.

Institute Leadership and Organizational Stewardship

  • Serve as a key member of DRI's executive leadership team and a strategic partner to the President in shaping institutional direction and priorities.
  • Collaborate closely with research division executive directors to align priorities, strengthen coordination, and advance shared institutional goals.
  • Work effectively with leaders across finance, advancement, communications, human resources, facilities, legal affairs, and technology to support the success of the research enterprise.
  • Contribute to enterprise-wide planning, resource allocation, policy development, and organizational decision-making.
  • Strengthen a culture of collaboration, transparency, accountability, and service across DRI.

Research Operations, Infrastructure, and Administrative Leadership

  • Provide executive oversight of DRI's research administration, compliance, computing, environmental health and safety, library, and research support functions.
  • Ensure effective stewardship of annual research expenditures and the resources that support DRI's research mission.
  • Develop and oversee the integrated budget for the Office of the Vice President for Research and related functions.
  • Maintain and strengthen research infrastructure, laboratories, computing capabilities, instrumentation, and support systems necessary for scientific excellence.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulations, sponsor requirements, institutional policies, and research integrity standards.

Measures of Success
The Vice President for Research will have the opportunity to shape the trajectory of one of the nation's most distinctive environmental research organizations. Success in this role will be reflected not only in the continued growth and competitiveness of DRI's research enterprise, but also in the Institute's ability to expand its influence, attract exceptional talent, strengthen strategic partnerships, and advance scientific discoveries that improve lives and inform solutions to critical environmental challenges.

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

  • Sustained growth in DRI's sponsored research portfolio through the expansion of federal, state, philanthropic, and private-sector funding opportunities.
  • Enhanced national visibility and recognition of DRI as a leading environmental research institution and trusted source of scientific expertise.
  • Strong relationships with federal and state agencies, policymakers, industry leaders, research institutions, and strategic partners that translate into new opportunities, collaborations, and institutional impact.
  • Increased interdisciplinary collaboration across DRI's research divisions, fostering innovative approaches to complex scientific and societal challenges.
  • Successful recruitment, retention, and development of exceptional scientific talent, with faculty and researchers equipped to thrive in DRI's entrepreneurial research environment.
  • Strategic investment in people, infrastructure, technology, and research support systems that strengthen the Institute's long-term competitiveness and capacity for growth.
  • Advancement of innovation, technology transfer, and other initiatives that expand the real-world impact of DRI's scientific discoveries.

The Candidate

Experience and Professional Qualifications
The Desert Research Institute seeks a distinguished scientific leader who combines scholarly credibility, strategic vision and foresight, and executive leadership with a demonstrated ability to advance research excellence, foster institutional growth, and build impactful partnerships. The ideal candidate will be an accomplished research executive who understands how to lead within a highly entrepreneurial, externally funded environment while cultivating a culture that empowers scientific innovation, collaboration, and discovery.

The successful candidate will bring a record of progressive leadership within complex research-intensive organizations and a demonstrated ability to navigate the evolving landscape of federally sponsored research, government relations, academic partnerships, and scientific innovation. This individual will possess the strategic perspective necessary to shape long-term research priorities while maintaining the operational discipline required to steward a significant research enterprise. Equally important, the Vice President for Research will be a relationship builder capable of engaging effectively with faculty, staff, agency leaders, elected officials, industry partners, philanthropic organizations, and other external stakeholders whose support is critical to advancing DRI's mission and impact.

DRI's next Vice President for Research must be equally comfortable serving as a scientific ambassador and institutional strategist. This leader will understand how to position research organizations for growth, identify emerging opportunities, strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration, and leverage external relationships to expand funding, influence, and impact. The ideal candidate will appreciate the distinctive nature of DRI's research model, where scientific excellence and entrepreneurial success are deeply intertwined, and will be energized by the opportunity to lead within an institution that combines the intellectual rigor of academia with the entrepreneurial mindset of a leading independent research enterprise.

The Vice President for Research will possess the judgment, credibility, intuitive leadership qualities and executive presence necessary to serve as a trusted advisor to the President and a respected leader within the scientific community. This individual will recognize that success in the role requires balancing scientific excellence, faculty support, research growth, institutional stewardship, and external engagement while advancing a shared vision for DRI's future.

The successful candidate will bring a combination of the following experiences and qualifications:

  • A distinguished record of achievement within a research-intensive organization, university, national laboratory, research institute, government agency, or similarly complex scientific enterprise.
  • Progressive executive leadership experience with responsibility for advancing research strategy, organizational growth, faculty or scientific talent, and institutional performance.
  • Demonstrated success leading large, complex, externally funded research enterprises and supporting investigators competing for federal, state, industry, and philanthropic funding opportunities.
  • A strong record of securing, managing, or overseeing significant sponsored research programs and research funding portfolios.
  • Experience fostering interdisciplinary research initiatives and building collaborations across scientific disciplines, organizations, and sectors.
  • Demonstrated success recruiting, mentoring, developing, and retaining high-performing scientists, faculty, researchers, and research leaders.
  • Experience developing and implementing strategic plans that strengthen research competitiveness, institutional impact, and long-term sustainability.
  • Proven ability to cultivate productive relationships with federal agencies, elected officials, policymakers, industry leaders, scientific organizations, donors, and strategic partners.
  • Demonstrated effectiveness serving as an external representative and advocate for a scientific or research organization.
  • Experience overseeing research administration, compliance, budgeting, infrastructure, technology, or related research support functions.
  • An understanding of research commercialization, technology transfer, innovation ecosystems, or public-private partnerships is desirable.
  • Experience operating within entrepreneurial or soft-funded research environments is strongly preferred.

Leadership Characteristics and Personal Attributes

The Vice President for Research demonstrates:

  • Strategic vision and foresight with the ability to anticipate emerging scientific, funding, and ever-changing technological, economic and policy trends while positioning DRI for future success.
  • An entrepreneurial mindset characterized by innovation, creativity, opportunity identification, and a commitment to growth.
  • Exceptional relationship-building, intuitive leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to foster trust among internal and external stakeholders.
  • A commitment to supporting faculty success and creating an environment where scientific excellence can thrive.
  • Strong executive presence and credibility with researchers, policymakers, funding agencies, governing bodies, and external partners.
  • Sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and an unwavering commitment to scientific integrity.
  • The ability to navigate complexity, balance competing priorities, and make thoughtful decisions.

Education
A Ph.D. or terminal degree from an accredited institution in a relevant scientific discipline is strongly preferred. Consideration may also be given to candidates with exceptional executive leadership experience within science, technology, research, or innovation organizations. Candidates must possess the scholarly credentials, professional stature, and scientific credibility necessary to lead a globally respected research enterprise.

The successful candidate must be a United States citizen and able to obtain and maintain a top security clearance.

Compensation
The minimum starting salary is $315,876 and will be competitive and commensurate with education, experience, and alignment with similar public academic research institutions. DRI provides excellent benefits that include:

  • Health insurance options that include dental, vision, life, and long-term disability.
  • 25% tax-deferred mandatory retirement contribution with matching by DRI.
  • Two (2) days of annual leave accrued each full month.
  • Thirty (30) days of sick leave provided upon start date and two (2) days of sick leave accrued per full month after the first year of service.
  • 12 paid holidays.
  • Tuition reduction at NSHE institutions for employee and eligible dependents.
  • No state income tax and no social security deduction.
  • Relocation assistance.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
DRI is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment free of discrimination without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, citizenship, age (40 or older), disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. DRI employs only U.S. citizens and persons lawfully authorized to work in the United States. Additionally, we comply with all applicable state laws and DRI takes measures consistent with Title IX to ensure the safety and wellbeing of its students, faculty and staff.

Application & Nominations
Applications should include a resume/CV to DRI-VPResearch@KornFerry.com Nominations and confidential inquiries are welcome.

Assistant Teaching Professor - Biomedical Engineering
Cornell University (Ithaca, NY)

The Nancy E. and Peter C. Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering at Cornell University has a full-time position for an Assistant Teaching Professor to teach and develop undergraduate and master’s level biomedical engineering courses. Teaching Professors are non-tenure track teaching faculty members who are hired on multi-year appointments with the expectation of renewal and promotion, with a 9-month service period plus summer opportunities. This position has an anticipated start date of Fall 2027. Teaching Professors in the Meinig School teach two 3-credit hour courses per semester and participate in faculty meetings, curricular review committees, and strategic planning.

The Meinig School is conducting two parallel faculty searches in biomedical engineering education. This Teaching Professor position is intended for educators who will provide leadership in undergraduate education through excellence and innovation in teaching, curriculum development, and student mentoring and advising; candidates will be evaluated primarily on the strength and potential of their teaching, educational leadership, and contributions to the biomedical engineering curriculum. In contrast, the school’s tenure-track discipline-based engineering education research (DBER) position is intended for scholars who will establish an independent, nationally recognized education research program, including mentoring Ph.D. students and postdoctoral scholars and advancing the field through innovative scholarship, external funding, and national leadership; candidates for that position will be evaluated on the strength and potential of their DBER scholarship.

A Ph.D. in bioengineering/biomedical engineering or closely related field is preferred with a record of outstanding teaching experience beyond the graduate teaching assistant level. Teaching experience aligned with one or more concentration areas within the biomedical engineering curriculum is expected, including but not limited to biomechanics, biomaterials, biomedical imaging, and cellular systems and computational biology.

Preference will be given to candidates with expertise in Machine Learning and/or Artificial Intelligence as applied to biomedical engineering. A strong commitment to undergraduate teaching and advising is essential. Teaching responsibilities will include participation in and development of both undergraduate and masters courses, and strong engagement in the biomedical engineering curriculum. Starting salary and title will depend upon the level of experience of the candidate.

The Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering is located in the College of Duffield Engineering on Cornell’s main campus in Ithaca, New York. Cornell University is an innovative Ivy League university and a great place to work. Tenure-track Faculty - Biomedical Engineering Education Research
Cornell University (Ithaca, NY)

Cornell University's Nancy E. and Peter C. Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering seeks applicants for a tenure-track faculty position in Engineering Education Research. The appointment is expected at the Assistant Professor level, but outstanding candidates at all ranks will be considered. Candidates must have an earned doctorate in engineering, STEM education, or a closely related field, with a demonstrated potential for success as an independent education research investigator and a classroom educator. Responsibilities include the pursuit of a program of scholarly research in Biomedical Engineering Education; teaching courses in Biomedical Engineering; and advising undergraduate and graduate students.

The Meinig School is conducting two parallel faculty searches in biomedical engineering education. This tenure-track discipline-based engineering education research (DBER) position is intended for scholars who will establish an independent, nationally recognized education research program, including mentoring Ph.D. students and postdoctoral scholars and advancing the field through innovative scholarship, external funding, and national leadership. In contrast, the School’s Teaching Professor position is intended for educators who will provide leadership in undergraduate education through excellence and innovation in teaching, curriculum development, and student mentoring and advising; candidates for that position will be evaluated primarily on the strength and potential of their teaching, educational leadership, and contributions to the biomedical engineering curriculum.

Candidates must show outstanding research and potential for excellence in teaching and research; senior candidates are expected to have exceptional accomplishments in research and teaching. We are especially interested in candidates who will contribute to the inclusive excellence of our academic community through their research, teaching, mentoring, and service. Salary and rank are commensurate with qualifications and experience.

The Meinig School of Biomedical Engineering is in the Duffield College of Engineering on Cornell’s campus in Ithaca, New York. Cornell has a growing community of scholars engaged in Engineering Education Research (EER) and Discipline-Based Education Research (DBER) across the sciences and engineering. The recently established Duffield Engineering Education Research Institute provides a community for and an institutional investment in research, collaboration, and action focused on how engineers learn, how innovation can shape educational systems, and how evidence can be used to improve teaching, learning, and the professional formation of engineers.

The BME department has a decades-long culture of educational innovation and outreach. Current efforts include engineering education research at the intersection of pedagogy, assessment, and generative AI methods; experiential and design-based learning major outreach programs to local-area middle- and high-school science teachers as well as science museums; and the integration of active learning throughout the biomedical engineering curriculum. Educational innovation is also a strategic priority across the Duffield College of Engineering and Cornell University.

Faculty engaged in discipline-based education research collaborate through the Duffield Engineering Education Research group, the Cornell Discipline-Based Education Research group, the McCormick Teaching Excellence Institute in Engineering, and the university-wide Center for Teaching Innovation and Active Learning Initiative. This community is filled with disciplinary experts who are passionate about their teaching, engaging in education research literature, and keen to discuss how to improve teaching and learning for students throughout multiple disciplines. The ideal candidate will benefit from strong collaborative ties to other discipline-based education researchers in the Duffield College of Engineering and across campus and to the major teaching/education centers, and will contribute to a culture of excellence in education research and of continual improvement in pedagogical approaches, both in their own teaching and through their work with faculty colleagues.

Qualified applicants should submit 1) a cover letter briefly summarizing background, qualifications, and interest in the position, 2) a Curriculum Vitae, 3) a research statement outlining experience, interests, and goals, 4) copies of three relevant publications, 5) a teaching statement outlining experience and philosophy, and 6) names and contact information for three references. Materials should be submitted online to: https://academicjobsonline.org/ajo/jobs/32596. Applications received by 1 November 2026 will be given full consideration. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

Inquires may be directed to: cornellbmesearch@cornell.edu

The Chandler Laboratory within the Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine at FIU/HWCOM is currently seeking a full-time, non-tenure Postdoctoral Associate position. The Department of Marine Biology (MARB) in the College of Marine Sciences & Maritime Studies at Texas A&M University located at the Galveston campus invites applications for one full-time, tenure-track faculty position with a 9-month academic appointment beginning August 1, 2027. This is a broad search for a dynamic marine biologist whose research advances understanding of marine organisms, habitats, or ecosystems at any spatial, temporal, or organizational scale, including molecular, cellular, physiological, organismal, population, community, ecosystem, seascape, ocean-basin, or global perspectives.

Applicants from all subdisciplines of marine biology are encouraged to apply. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, disturbance and disease ecology, benthic pollution and emerging contaminants, species management (e.g., birds, corals, endangered species), ecosystem management and restoration, and soundscapes. The successful candidate will establish and maintain a rigorous, sustainable, externally funded research program with national and international impact. Particular consideration will be given to candidates whose research complements the department’s existing strengths and leverages the extensive resources and collaborative opportunities available within the Department of Marine Biology, the Galveston campus, and across the Texas A&M University System. The candidate will seek to foster interdisciplinary collaborations with local, regional, national, or international science, management, conservation, industry, education, and/or stakeholder communities.

The Department of Marine Biology provides a distinctive educational environment that integrates classroom instruction, laboratory training, field experience, and research mentorship. The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate education by teaching existing courses and/or developing innovative offerings aligned with the candidate’s expertise and departmental needs based on the programs’ curricula. The successful candidate will mentor undergraduate research interns and graduate students and contribute to a learning environment that prepares students for careers in research, conservation, management, education, policy, and the broader blue economy.

The successful candidate will also contribute service to the department, college, university, profession, and broader community. Service may include committee participation, engagement with professional societies, contributions to student mentoring and career-development activities, outreach to marine-science stakeholders, and participation in programs that strengthen the visibility and impact of marine biology at Texas A&M University at Galveston.

Texas A&M University at Galveston is the dedicated marine and maritime branch campus of Texas A&M University. The campus houses several institutions that are critical contributors to Texas A&M’s land-, sea-, and space-grant mission and drives the development of the blue economy on the Gulf Coast through education, innovation, scholarship and research.

Home to the Texas A&M College of Marine Sciences & Maritime Studies (marine.tamu.edu), students can earn undergraduate and graduate degrees in marine sciences, business, blue humanities, marine engineering and maritime transportation. Students may also pursue select Galveston-specific Texas A&M College of Engineering degrees, including computer science, ocean engineering and interdisciplinary engineering.

Texas A&M-Galveston is also home to the Texas A&M Maritime Academy, one of six state maritime academies in the U.S. and the only one embedded within a Tier I research institution. Offering hands-on training to over 400 cadets annually, the academy prepares students to earn a U.S. Coast Guard License and serve as maritime professionals, afloat and ashore, or enter military service upon graduation.

Ideally situated in Galveston Bay, the island campus is surrounded by marine life, estuarine and ocean ecosystems, and one of the largest maritime industrial hubs in the world, allowing Galveston Aggies to live, learn and work in the heart of the industries they will soon serve. Whether their careers take them shoreside or on the water, Aggies are ready for anything above, on and below the waves.

Texas A&M University is committed to enriching the learning and working environments for all visitors, students, faculty, and staff, which is vital to accomplishing our mission and living our core values.

  • Candidate must have earned a Ph.D. in marine biology, biology, ecology, evolution, oceanography, environmental science, fisheries science, or a related field.
  • Applicants should demonstrate evidence of research productivity, potential for extramural funding, commitment to effective teaching and mentorship, and capacity to contribute collegially to an interdisciplinary academic community.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Postdoctoral or equivalent professional research experience is preferred.

Application Instructions

Applicants must submit electronic PDF copies of i) cover letter, ii) curriculum vitae, iii) personal statements to include research plans (3 pages), teaching statement describing instructional experience, mentoring philosophy, and potential course contributions (1 page) and service (1 page), and iv) names and contact information of three (3) professional references by applying online at: https://apply.interfolio.com/188456.

Questions or inquiries about the position should be directed to Dr. Jessica Labonté, chair of the search committee at labontej@tamu.edu. Applications are due by October 15, 2026 and the position will remain open until filled.

Our commitment to employment equity helps achieve inclusion and fairness, brings rich diversity to UBC as a workplace, and creates the necessary conditions for a rewarding career.

The Department of Cellular and Physiological Sciences at The University of British Columbia (UBC) invites applications for a Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader in Health and Biotechnology, with focus in Multiparametric Physiologic Metabolism. The successful candidate will be appointed to a tenure-track faculty position.

The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a one-time initiative designed to support institutions in attracting internationally based Early Career Researchers to Canada. Emerging Leaders will receive research funding and institutional supports to advance transformative research in Canada’s strategic priority areas, build partnerships across sectors and borders, and translate their research into applications and impacts that benefit Canadians and the world. Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders are six-year positions valued at $100,000 annually, renewable once for an additional six years, intended for exceptional emerging scholars who have the potential to lead in their fields. Applicants must be early-career researchers and be eligible to hold a full-time, tenure-stream appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor at UBC.

Under the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program, nominees must be working and residing outside Canada when the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada award (https://www.canada.ca/en/impact-plus-chairs.html) is formally accepted (July 1st 2026). Applicants may apply regardless of their current location; however, candidates selected for nomination must meet this eligibility requirement on the award acceptance date in order to proceed. Expatriate Canadians wishing to relocate to Canada are welcome to apply.

The Department of Cellular and Physiological Sciences (www.cellphys.ubc.ca), part of the UBC Faculty of Medicine, is internationally recognized for using diverse approaches and model systems to investigate the fundamental cellular and physiological mechanisms underlying human health and disease.

The Department is seeking an outstanding early-career basic and/or translational scientist with expertise in metabolism. We take a broad view of the field and welcome applications from individuals working on metabolism at, or across, different biological scales using diverse model systems and innovative approaches. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, cellular and molecular metabolism, metabolic regulation within and between organs/tissues, energy balance and homeostasis, nutrient sensing and signaling, hormonal, genetic, and environmental regulation of metabolism, inter-organ communication, systems physiology, metabolic adaptations across the lifespan, metabolic dysregulation in disease, and determinants of metabolic resilience.

The Department is located in the Life Sciences Institute (LSI), which is made up of over 80 primary investigators and research groups. The LSI, has outstanding space and core facilities and is a leader in interdisciplinary and innovative research aimed at understanding fundamental mechanisms of human health and environmental sustainability (www.lsi.ubc.ca). The Department and LSI are well positioned within the basic science and clinical communities and offer potential interactions with groups such as the Stem Cell Network of Canada, Genome BC, and the Metabolomics Consortium of British Columbia, as well as the Cellular and Regenerative Medicine Centre, Diabetes Research Group, Women’s Health Research Institute, at BC Children's Hospital Research Institute.

The successful candidate will be expected to

Develop an internationally recognized research program Attract and manage external funding for their research program Mentor postdoctoral fellows, graduate, and undergraduate students Contribute to the newly-developed undergraduate program www.cps.med.ubc.ca/undergraduate-program Contribute to a graduate program that is affiliated with our department Engage in service for the department, faculty, and university affiliated with the Department of Cellular and Physiological Sciences, as well as the greater academic and scientific community.

Required Qualifications

Candidates must have:

  • A PhD, MD/PhD, MD or equivalent in the biological or biomedical sciences, as part of the UBC requirement.
  • A developing record of research excellence.
  • A strong commitment to excellence in teaching.
  • Demonstrated a willingness to respect diverse perspectives and skills related to respect, equity, diversity and inclusion.

The expected salary for this position is $150,000 per annum. The Faculty of Medicine is committed to offering equitable and competitive salaries, commensurate with the qualifications and experience of the candidate. The Institute for Medical Engineering and Science (IMES) http://imes.mit.edu/ at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), in Cambridge, Massachusetts, invites applicants to apply for tenure-track faculty positions in all areas of science and engineering with application to health sciences to begin July 1, 2027 or on a mutually agreed date thereafter. Established in 2012, IMES is an inclusive community of students, administrative staff, research staff, and faculty who research, work, educate, and learn, at the convergence of engineering, science, and medicine to transform human health for all.

Appointment will be at the assistant professor level. In special cases, however, an untenured associate or senior faculty appointment may be possible, commensurate with experience. The appointment will be made in partnership with a relevant science or engineering department. The position will have equal academic responsibilities in IMES and the partner department. Applicants must hold an MD or a PhD in a science or engineering field related to health sciences by the beginning of employment. While all research areas are of interest, IMES encourages applications from candidates whose research and teaching interests would be enhanced and accelerated through deep engagement with both basic and clinical partners, and whose research program intimately involves the development and/or application of advanced computational methods. Examples include, but are not limited to:

  • Clinical data generation, analysis, and sharing to improve health care delivery;
  • The development, testing, and analysis of devices, sensors, & interfaces (mechanical, optical, electrical, chemical), and their products, to advance health care and its delivery;
  • Methods and modeling to understand the impact of environmental shifts on human health;
  • Deriving insights into human diseases through epidemiological research and mechanistic modeling;
  • Improving our ability to understand, predict, and manipulate human immune responses (e.g., in the context of infectious diseases, neuro-immune interactions, or women’s health)

The successful candidate will be expected to fulfill all teaching, research, and service obligations of a tenure-track faculty member at MIT. Faculty duties include teaching courses in both the candidate’s home science/engineering department and in Health Science & Technology at the undergraduate and graduate levels, advising students, conducting original scholarly research, developing course materials at the graduate and undergraduate levels, and service to MIT and the profession.

Interested candidates should submit application materials electronically at https://faculty searches.mit.edu/imes-search/. Each application must include: a curriculum vitae; the names and addresses of three or more references; a strategic statement of research interests; a statement of teaching interests; and three representative recent publications. It is the responsibility of the candidate to arrange for reference letters to be uploaded at https://faculty-searches.mit.edu/imes-search/letters/.

Please address questions to imes-search@mit.edu. Complete application materials received by December 1, 2026 will be given priority.

MIT is an equal employment opportunity employer. We value diversity and strongly encourage applications from individuals from all identities and backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive equitable consideration for employment based on their experience and qualifications and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, religion, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, ancestry, or national or ethnic origin. See MIT’s full policy on Nondiscrimination (https://policies.mit.edu/policies-procedures/90-relations-and responsibilities-within-mit-community/92-nondiscrimination). Know your rights: see https://www.eeoc.gov/sites/default/files/2022 10/EEOC_KnowYourRights_screen_reader_10_20.pdf.

description:
Indiana University Bloomington (IUB) invites applications for an open-rank, tenured/tenure-track faculty position in the School of Public Health-Bloomington in the field of Aging and Technology. We seek candidates to join IU’s outstanding research enterprise in aging and gerontology and collaborate in areas such as social and behavioral science, digital health, behavioral epidemiology, bio-health informatics, human factors, robotics, implementation science, and neuroscience.

The position is part of Indiana University's Faculty 100 initiative, a strategic investment in exceptional scholars whose work advances the university's research excellence and national impact.

We encourage applications from scholars who bring interdisciplinary perspectives and whose research complements existing strengths at Indiana University, while introducing new directions that expand and strengthen the institution’s research capacity in aging and technology.

This 10‐month appointment begins August 1, 2027, although an earlier or later start date is negotiable. Applications received by October 16, 2026, will receive full consideration, and applications will be accepted until the positions are filled.

Responsibilities

Tenured/tenure-track faculty at Indiana University Bloomington are expected to contribute substantially to the university’s missions of research, teaching, and service. Responsibilities include:

  • Developing and maintaining an externally funded and nationally recognized research program;
  • Pursuing and securing major extramural funding as principal investigator and collaborative investigator;
  • Publishing impactful scholarship in leading peer-reviewed outlets;
  • Teaching and mentoring undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students;
  • Engaging in interdisciplinary collaboration across Indiana University and with external partners; and
  • Providing service and leadership within the department, school, university, profession, and community.

Candidates with special interest in any of the following (or related) areas are encouraged to apply:

  • Wearable & Ambient Sensors: Continuous physiological and behavioral monitoring; fall detection and prediction; dementia care and wandering prevention; activity tracking for chronic disease management.
  • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning: Predictive risk modeling for falls, hospitalization, and cognitive decline; Natural Language Processing (NLP) for remote cognitive assessment; image analysis for wound care; condition prediction and diagnosis.
  • Conversational AI & Social Robotics: Companionship for socially isolated or lonely older adults; medication reminders for adherence; caregiver-facing information and guidance systems.
  • Telehealth & Remote Monitoring: Chronic disease management; specialist access for rural populations; post-acute monitoring to prevent readmissions.
  • Smart Home Technologies: Automated safety systems for dementia patients; environmental controls for mobility-limited adults; passive monitoring without wearables.
  • Digital Biomarkers: Passively collected behavioral data from consumer devices enabling detection of cognitive decline, mood changes, and functional deterioration years before clinical presentation.
  • Extended Reality (XR / VR): Pain management, cognitive rehabilitation, physical therapy engagement, and social connection for homebound and institutionalized older adults.

This position is located on the Bloomington campus of Indiana University. Successful candidates are expected to work on campus to allow full engagement with the department, school, university, and community. Indiana University bases tenure and promotion recommendations upon performance in research, teaching, and service. Faculty hired through this initiative are expected to excel in research and demonstrate strong performance in teaching and service.

The successful candidate will contribute to and help expand Indiana University's nationally recognized aging research enterprise. The individual will have opportunities to collaborate broadly across Indiana University schools, centers, and institutes, including the Regenstrief Institute, the Irsay Institute, the Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering, the School of Medicine, the School of Nursing, and other units engaged in aging, health, technology, and data science research. The position is intended to catalyze innovative interdisciplinary partnerships, support multi-investigator research initiatives, and strengthen Indiana University's competitiveness for large-scale federal, foundation, and industry-funded research programs.

Minimum Qualifications

Applicants must hold an earned doctoral degree in public health, behavioral science, social science, data science, informatics, engineering, neuroscience, rehabilitation science, health services research, or a closely related field by the date of appointment and demonstrate a commitment to excellence in research, teaching, mentoring, and service, appropriate to rank.

Candidates for tenured positions must demonstrate a record of scholarly achievement appropriate for an appointment with tenure, including extramurally funded research as a principal investigator, current funding or strong potential to secure external funding, an established record of publications and scholarly contributions, and experience leading significant research initiatives.

Application Procedures

Review of applications will begin October 16, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Application materials should include:

  • Cover letter (1 page maximum)
  • Current Curriculum Vitae
  • Research & Teaching Statement (maximum of 3 pages describing research experience and future goals, and an additional 2 pages on teaching and mentorship experience)
  • Up to three representative scholarly publications (optional)
  • Contact information for three professional references
    • Professional references will only be solicited for candidates selected for a finalist interview and/or job offer.

Applicants should apply at: https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34281

Questions regarding the position or application process may be directed to Dr. Matthew Lee Smith, Search Committee Chair (matlsmit@iu.edu), or Dr. Cindy Broderick, Search Coordinator, at faculty1@indiana.edu.

Before a conditional offer of employment with tenure is finalized, candidates will be asked to disclose any pending investigations or previous findings of sexual or professional misconduct. Candidates will also be required to authorize Indiana University Bloomington to inquire with current and former employers regarding such matters. The relevance of information disclosed or obtained during this process to a candidate’s eligibility for hire will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis. Indiana University Bloomington takes matters of sexual and professional misconduct very seriously.

Indiana University is an equal opportunity employer and provider of ADA services and prohibits discrimination in hiring. See Indiana University Notice of Non-Discrimination here which includes contact information.

About the School of Public Health-Bloomington

The Indiana University School of Public Health-Bloomington (SPH-B) is one of the nation's leading schools of public health and is committed to advancing health and well-being through excellence in research, teaching, service, and community engagement. Located on Indiana University's flagship campus, SPH-B includes five academic departments and more than 300 faculty and staff dedicated to addressing complex public health challenges through innovative, interdisciplinary approaches.

The School is home to nationally and internationally recognized scholars whose work spans public health, health behavior, epidemiology, environmental health, aging, health policy, physical activity, recreation, nutrition, and health technology. Faculty collaborate widely across Indiana University and with partners throughout the state, nation, and world to improve population health and well-being.

The successful candidate will join the Department of Applied Health Science, a nationally recognized department committed to improving health and well-being through research, teaching, and community engagement. Faculty conduct interdisciplinary research across aging and gerontology, health behavior, chronic disease prevention and management, dementia and Alzheimer's disease, sexuality and reproductive health, nutrition, physical activity, substance use, community health, implementation science, and health equity. The department has particular strengths in aging and gerontology, including research focused on dementia and Alzheimer's disease, caregiving, chronic disease prevention and management, falls prevention, health behavior change, and technology enabled approaches to improve health and quality of life among older adults.

The School of Public Health-Bloomington is an ideal academic home for a scholar in Aging and Technology. Faculty within SPH-B are conducting innovative research in aging, chronic disease prevention and management, dementia and Alzheimer's disease, caregiving, falls prevention, digital health, and technology-enabled approaches to improve health and quality of life among older adults. This position will strengthen and expand Indiana University's substantial aging research ecosystem and multidisciplinary Aging Research Network.

Indiana University provides faculty with exceptional support for teaching, scholarship, and research through programs such as the Faculty Academy on Excellence in Teaching (F.A.C.E.T.), extensive research development and administrative support through the Office of the Vice President for Research, and a rich culture of interdisciplinary collaboration. Faculty have opportunities to collaborate across Indiana University with leading scholars in public health, data science and artificial intelligence, bio-health informatics, neuroscience, nursing, medicine, pharmacy, human factors, rehabilitation sciences, environmental sciences, engineering, robotics, and social work.

About Indiana University Bloomington

Founded in 1820, Indiana University-Bloomington (IUB) is the flagship campus of Indiana University and a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU). With more than 47,000 students and 16 degree-granting schools and colleges, IU Bloomington offers an exceptional environment for academic excellence, innovation, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Located in south-central Indiana, Bloomington combines the resources of a world-class research university with the quality of life of a vibrant college town. The community offers a rich arts and cultural environment, outstanding outdoor recreation opportunities, excellent schools, and an affordable cost of living.

  • Indiana University Bloomington: Indiana University Bloomington

Description

Join us at EIT:

At the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT), we're on a mission to translate scientific discovery into real world impact. We bring together visionary scientists, technologists, engineers, researchers, educators and innovators to tackle humanity's greatest challenges in four transformative areas:

  • Health, Medical Science & Generative Biology
  • Food Security & Sustainable Agriculture
  • Climate Change & Managing CO2
  • Artificial Intelligence & Robotics


This is ambitious work - work that demands curiosity, courage, and a relentless drive to make a difference. At EIT, you'll join a community built on excellence, innovation, tenacity, trust, and collaboration, where bold ideas become real-world breakthroughs. Together, we push boundaries, embrace complexity, and create solutions to scale ideas from lab to society. Explore more at www.eit.org .

Your Role:

This is an exciting opportunity for a highly efficient Administrator to support the Student Engagement team within the EIT Education & Scholarships team. The Education & Scholarships team works with undergraduate and graduate students funded to study at the University of Oxford and connected to EIT projects, developing and deploying technology for global benefit.

The Student Engagement functional area supports EIT-funded students to develop their potential and thrive on an elevated trajectory as future innovators and leaders. We lead a high-touch onboarding journey, coordinate a fully integrated internship programme for undergraduate students, deliver structured skills programming and experiential learning and cultivate a vibrant, connected student community.

The role will provide broad administrative and operational support across the team, with a particular focus on supporting the coordination and delivery of student events and programming. Some out-of-hours work will be required, particularly during student events requiring a flexible professional with strong interpersonal skills, exceptional organisational skills and experience working in a diverse setting.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Support the planning and delivery of student events and programming, coordinating registrations, venues, catering, accessibility requirements, event materials and on-the-day logistics.
  • Coordinate event communications, including invitations, reminders, logistical updates and post-event follow-up, and respond to routine attendee enquiries.
  • Manage the team inbox and other communication channels, coordinating timely responses and follow-up with relevant teams, and escalating complex or sensitive matters as appropriate.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date student records and support the day-to-day administration of processes in Salesforce and other relevant systems, completing routine data entry and quality checks, resolving discrepancies, and escalating system issues or enhancement needs.
  • Maintain event documentation and support evaluation, including attendance records, feedback surveys and evaluation data.
  • Support venue and supplier administration, including supplier onboarding, contract documentation, raising purchase orders and tracking invoices.
  • Coordinate the development and review of key student materials, such as the Student Handbook, ensuring content is accessible and engaging.
  • Provide administrative and logistical support for meetings, including scheduling, agenda preparation, minute-taking, and follow-up of agreed actions.
  • Provide general administrative assistance to the Student Engagement team as required, contributing to a well-functioning team.


Requirements

Essential Skills, Qualifications & Experience:

  • Experience supporting the logistical aspects of events, meetings and projects.
  • Strong verbal and written communication with exceptional interpersonal skills
  • Strong cultural awareness and sensitivity, with the ability to work with people from a variety of backgrounds.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Demonstrable administrative experience, including managing enquiries, coordinating follow-up actions and maintaining accurate records.
  • Technically proficient in Microsoft Office, with confidence in learning and using a CRM and other administrative systems.
  • Ability to manage a varied and high-volume workload in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated commitment to the highest standards of ethics and confidentiality.
  • Experience supporting multiple stakeholders.


Desirable Knowledge, Skills and Experience

  • At least two years' experience in an administrative role.
  • Experience using Salesforce or a comparable CRM system.
  • Experience working and communicating with students and/or young people, particularly within an education, scholarship or similar environment.


Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

  • Salary - Up to £35,000 (dependent on experience) + travel allowance + bonus
  • Enhanced holiday. Our annual leave allowance is 25 days plus 8 bank holidays and an additional 3 days between Christmas and New Year. You will also have the opportunity to purchase an additional 5 days annual leave in January and July.
  • Pension - Employer contribution 7.5%, minimum employee contribution 5%
  • Life Assurance.
  • Income Protection
  • Private Medical Insurance as standard for you, your partner and any dependents. Including hospital Cash Plan
  • Employee discounts
  • Electric car scheme
  • Nursery Salary Sacrifice scheme
  • Cycle to Work Scheme
  • Family Planning
  • Neurodiversity support including advise and assessments
  • Coaching & Therapy services


Working Together - What It Involves:

  • You must have the right to work permanently in the UK with a willingness to travel as necessary. We do not offer sponsorship for this role.
  • You will live in, or within easy commuting distance of, Oxford (or be willing to relocate) and can commit to our hybrid working model.
  • Please note, the closing date for applications is Tuesday 29th September 2026.

Welcome to the Plant Biology Institute:

The Plant Biology Institute, headed by Professor Steve Kelly, is a key part of the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT) Oxford. The institute aims to develop impactful and commercially sustainable solutions for improving global food production and planetary health through pioneering plant science research.

The Plant Biology Institute will unite world-class researchers who are focused on expanding the frontiers of plant science. Our research is focused on enhancing our ability to feed the planet while simultaneously improving the climate and ecosystem outcomes of food production. By embedding cutting-edge plant science research within an organisation that is focused on solving global challenges at scale, we aim to accelerate the timeline from discovery to global impact.

Areas of exploration include:

  • Improved plant productivity, both indoors and outside.
  • Reduced reliance on inputs including water, fertilisers, pesticides, and herbicides.
  • Novel decarbonised plant-based production platforms for food and medicines.
  • Advanced technologies that speed up discovery and deployment in plants.


Researchers will have access to state-of-the-art laboratory and plant growth facilities and have opportunities to collaborate with experts at the forefront of research on AI, automation, and generative biology across the EIT ecosystem. They will also work with global leaders in market development, commercialisation, and impact creation. The Plant Biology Institute has long-term substantial funding to support the unique scale and ambition of its vision.

Your Role:

EIT is seeking a highly motivated and skilled Scientist or Senior Scientist in Plant Metabolic Engineering to join its pioneering Plant Biology Institute.

The successful candidate will lead the development of innovative metabolic engineering and synthetic biology approaches to manipulate plant cellular conditions. Specifically, the candidate will design, implement and characterise engineering strategies to optimise plant respiratory activity, energy status, and redox balance. These engineering approaches will be first evaluated and optimised in plant cell cultures guided by iterative design-build-test-learn cycles before being translated into whole plants for improving productivity.

The scientist will be expected to contribute to IP generation and play an active role in translating research into real-world and commercial solutions aligned with EIT's mission of humane technological advancement. This role offers a unique opportunity to conduct high-impact research at the forefront of plant science while collaborating across multidisciplinary teams to drive innovation from lab to global impact.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Design, implement and characterise engineering strategies to manipulate plant respiratory activity, energy status, and redox balance

Facet Amtech is developing a world-first clean ammonia process — producing ammonia directly from air and water, without the hydrogen infrastructure (SMR or electrolysers) that conventional grey, blue and green ammonia plants require. Our process feeds air and water into a reactor where the catalyst simultaneously separates hydrogen from water and reduces nitrogen from the air, combining the two directly into ammonia. This removes major plant infrastructure costs, improves energy efficiency by avoiding generated waste heat, and drives production costs below grey ammonia prices.

We are seeking an exceptional Principal Scientist to drive this technology forward. Leading the R&D team and reporting to the CEO, you will provide scientific direction across catalyst development, process integration and pilot-scale technology development. This is a role for someone who wants to bring cutting-edge research into the real world, contributing directly to global decarbonisation and sustainable industrial development. As Facet Amtech grows, this role is expected to play a key part in building and leading the future of our catalyst and process development capabilities.

Working with the science and engineering team, you will contribute across catalyst development, manufacturing, material characterisation and process integration; feedstock and product gas characterisation; analysis and interpretation of experimental data; and development of reliable, repeatable experiment protocols and quality control. The role requires hands-on laboratory work to translate fundamental research into larger-scale projects — a unique opportunity to work on complex technical problems that demands a high level of attention to detail and the tenacity to identify and resolve unexpected system behaviours.

We’re based in Newcastle, one of Australia’s fastest-growing energy transition hubs, having recently moved into an independent facility to accelerate lab-based R&D, catalyst manufacturing scale-up and pilot work. The region combines a strong industrial and research base with a coastal lifestyle, easy access to the Hunter Valley, and a cost of living well below Australia’s capital cities.

Key Responsibilities

Scientific Leadership

  • Provide scientific leadership across catalyst, reactor and process development activities.
  • Drive a culture of intellectual curiosity, scientific rigor, critical thinking and evidence-based decision making.
  • Undertake technical reviews and scientific decision-making processes across the organisation.
  • Develop technical reports, summaries and strategic recommendations.
  • Establish clear technical priorities and development objectives.

Scientific Analysis and Problem Solving

  • Guide catalyst synthesis, screening, optimisation and scale-up activities.
  • Apply materials science and chemistry principles by performing characterisation experiments to develop mechanistic understanding of catalyst behaviour and performance.
  • Ensure experimental procedures, data, analyses and conclusions are appropriately documented and traceable.
  • Apply first-principles thinking to challenge assumptions, identify root causes of behaviours, and progress technical development.
  • Critically evaluate experimental design, data quality and interpretation.
  • Support theoretical model development in line with thermodynamic, kinetic and process constraints.
  • Translate catalyst requirements into reactor operating conditions and testing methodologies.
  • Work with the R&D and engineering teams to develop bench-scale and continuous operation pilot-scale systems.

Essential Qualifications & Experience

  • PhD or equivalent industry experience in Chemistry, Materials Science, Chemical Engineering or a closely related discipline.
  • Deep expertise in heterogeneous catalysis, catalytic materials and reaction mechanisms.
  • Strong understanding of catalyst characterisation techniques and interpretation.
  • Proven ability to solve highly complex, multidisciplinary scientific problems.
  • Experience leading research programs within small technical teams.
  • Strong experimental design and data analysis skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Desirable Experience

  • Ammonia synthesis, nitrogen activation, hydrogenation catalysis or related technologies.
  • Technology scale-up from laboratory to pilot or full-scale operation.
  • Industrial R&D, technology development, start-up or scale-up environments.
  • Theoretical catalyst/process modelling (DFT, CFD, reactor modelling, thermodynamics/kinetics, process simulation packages).
