Program Highlights

1. Duration: Our joint postdoctoral program has a duration of four years, with an equal distribution of time between MPG and WIS. This unique structure allows postdoctoral fellows to benefit from the expertise and resources available at both institutions, fostering a rich and diverse research experience by ensuring dedicated time for in-depth exploration, comprehensive experimentation and significant contributions to their respective fields.

2. Eligibility Criteria:

a. Applicants must start the program within 4 years of their Ph.D. graduation

b.Current WIS postdocs are eligible to apply, but must commence the program before the end of their first year at WIS

c. Commencement into the program is contingent upon PhD thesis submission

3. Fellowships: During their time at MPG, postdocs positions are according to the German regulations and guidelines, and based on the experience level (German level 2 or level 3).

Specific annual taxable salary levels are €67,311 for level 2 and €72,800 for level 3.

This includes benefits such as health insurance, nursing care insurance, vacation days, pension insurance, and unemployment insurance.

During their time at WIS, postdocs will receive an untaxed fellowship of 212,088 NIS annually for level 2 and 220,920 NIS annually for level 3.

* Postdoctoral fellows in Israel are exempt from taxes.

In addition, at WIS, Postdocs will receive full family health insurance, nursing care subsidy, vacation days, relocation expenses and subsidized housing.

The relocation expenses will be paid by the host Institution to which the fellow is relocating, and up to twice during the program (with a minimum of 18 months in between). The expenses are at the level of €1500 for single postdocs per relocation, and €3000 for postdocs with spouses and families.

4. Global Research Collaboration: Fellows will have the opportunity to collaborate with leading scientists from both MPG and WIS. This program promotes a global research network, facilitating the exchange of ideas, expertise and diverse perspectives.

5. Independent Travel Support: We understand the importance of scientific networking and dissemination of research findings. As part of this program, fellows will receive up to 3000 Euros per year for conferences, workshops and seminars, enabling them to present their work, engage with peers, and establish valuable professional connections.

Application Process

To apply for the MPG-WIS Joint Postdoctoral Program, please follow the application guidelines below:

  1. Contact researchers at MPG (see list of institutions; https://www.weizmann.ac.il/sites/mpg-wis/application-process#block-wis-theme-views-block-list-of-mpg-institutions-block-1) and at WIS; (https://www.weizmann.ac.il/pages/science/research), to discuss potential collaborative projects for which the researchers from both institutions can serve as joint hosts.
  2. Provide a detailed CV highlighting your academic background, research experience, list of publications, list of invited talks, awards, and any other relevant information specific to your field of research.
  3. Arrange for at least three letters of recommendation (one should be from the PhD advisor). These letters should come from individuals familiar with your research work and can assess your potential as a postdoctoral researcher in your specific field.
  4. Support letters from the MPG and WIS host researchers (can be a joint letter). Please note: as at each institute the costs are split between the institute and the PI, the PIs should declare that they have available funds to support the candidate.
  5. A Research statement explaining the project and its collaborative nature between the MPG and WIS (Length: up to 2 pages, Margins: 2 cm, Font size: 11 pt)
  6. A statement about the planned split between the institutes (MPG and WIS) for the duration of the 4 years. This should indicate at which institute (MPG or WIS) you will begin your four-year position. The four years should be split equally between the institutions. Several transfers are allowed, but generally not for a duration of less than a year. This plan should be based on scientific justification given the expertise and infrastructure at both institutions. This plan can be changed during the program upon the program committee approval.
  7. Upon completing the session and clicking the “Submit Application” button, you will receive an email verifying your application. Please note: this email also contains unique links for each of the referees you have listed. You may send each referee their unique link, which will allow them to access the system and submit their letter of recommendation.

For inquiries and assistance regarding the joint postdoctoral program offered by the MPG and WIS, please reach out to our program coordinator, Ms. Livnat Moses.

Livnat will be your main point of contact and will provide guidance throughout the application process and during your participation in the program.

You can contact the program coordinator via the following channels:

Email: postdoc@weizmann.ac.il

Phone: +972-8-9343842

December 21, 2026, for positions starting between March 2027 and September 2027.

Host-Pathogen Interactions / Inflammation / Immunity

Postdoctoral research positions are available for highly motivated candidates to investigate inflammation and innate immunity in the skin during viral infections and chronic/recurring diseases, including cancer. Experimental models will include in vitro assays, conventional and organoid cell cultures, knockout/transgenic mice, transcriptomics, and gene editing. description:
Faculty Position- in Biology and Biological Engineering: Caltech, Pasadena, CA, United States


The Division of Biology and Biological Engineering (BBE) at Caltech is seeking a faculty member in the area of Molecular Cell Biology. We are interested in candidates who will establish an innovative, interdisciplinary research program studying fundamental processes in any area of molecular cell biology. These include, but are not limited to, candidates with a research focus in:
(i) mechanistic studies of cellular processes (translation, membrane trafficking, signal transduction, cytoskeleton, gene regulation, biomolecular condensates, etc.)
(ii) quantitative or computational modeling of cellular processes.
(iii) molecular and cellular characterizations related to specific fields (virology, immunology, stem cell biology, etc.)

Successful candidates may also leverage or develop advanced quantitative techniques such as live imaging, cryo-electron microscopy, proteomics, genomics, synthetic biology, or AI-based analysis and prediction coupled with more classical methods such as biochemistry and genetics to push the boundaries of mechanistic discovery in cell biology. This position offers the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines and contribute to a dynamic research environment aimed at addressing key biological and biomedical challenges.

Successful applicants are expected to develop innovative research programs and to demonstrate a strong commitment to teaching and mentorship at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Preference will be given to candidates at the Assistant Professor level; however, well-qualified applicants at the associate or full professor level may also be considered. The term of an initial untenured appointment is for four years and is contingent upon completion of the Ph.D. degree.

Please submit on-line applications at: https://www.bbe.caltech.edu/jobs and include a brief cover letter, curriculum vitae, relevant publications, and a description of proposed research. In addition, applicants should submit an education statement that addresses the applicant’s thoughts on classroom and laboratory instruction, mentorship of students and postdoctoral scholars, and ways to foster an inclusive environment for the development of scholars who come to Caltech with many different perspectives and experiences

Applicants should arrange to have 3-4 reference letters uploaded.

Salaries for professorial faculty at Caltech fall in the range $125,000-$400,000.

Applications submitted by October 16, 2026 will be given full consideration.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

description:
The Division of Medicinal Chemistry and Pharmacognosy in the College of Pharmacy at The Ohio State University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level.

This position is part of Ohio State’s university-wide AI (X) Hub, a multidisciplinary initiative that brings together researchers across 15 colleges to advance artificial intelligence for the public good. The AI (X) Hub is expanding the university’s research community through the recruitment of 100 AI-focused faculty members and is organized around six strategic pillars, including AI for Health.

We seek an innovative scientist who will establish an independent, externally funded research program that harnesses artificial intelligence to advance drug discovery and therapeutic development. The successful candidate will apply approaches such as machine learning, deep learning, generative modeling, and other emerging computational methods to address fundamental and translational challenges in the pharmaceutical sciences.

We welcome applicants whose research focuses on one or more of the following areas:

Small-molecule drug discovery: AI-enabled molecular design and optimization, virtual screening, and prediction of efficacy, toxicity, ADME, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic properties. Protein and peptide design: Computational approaches to de novo design, structure and function prediction, and optimization of therapeutic proteins and peptides. Chemical biology: AI-enabled design and application of chemical probes to interrogate biological systems, elucidate mechanisms of action, validate therapeutic targets, and advance drug discovery. Biosynthetic engineering: AI-enabled design, optimization, and engineering of biosynthetic pathways, enzymes, and microbial or cellular systems for the discovery and production of natural products, biopharmaceuticals, and other therapeutic molecules. Candidates whose research bridges these areas or introduces complementary and emerging applications of AI in drug discovery and chemical biology are strongly encouraged to apply.

Collaborative Environment

The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative environment within the Division of Medicinal Chemistry and Pharmacognosy and the broader College of Pharmacy. As a member of the AI (X) Hub, the faculty member will have opportunities to work with AI researchers, medicinal chemists, structural biologists, pharmaceutical scientists, biomedical investigators, clinicians, and industry partners across Ohio State.

The position will contribute to the AI (X) Hub’s AI for Health mission by developing innovative, responsible, and translational AI approaches that accelerate therapeutic discovery and improve human health. The university’s AI for Health initiative is designed to connect advances in AI with biomedical research, clinical needs, and real-world health applications.

Key Facilities and Core Services

The successful candidate will have access to advanced drug discovery infrastructure and expertise through the Drug Discovery Shared Resource, or DDSR, and its medicinal chemistry and high-throughput screening capabilities within The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center – James Cancer Hospital and Solove Research Institute, or OSUCCC – James.

The DDSR integrates expertise in medicinal and synthetic chemistry, chemical biology, instrumental analysis, molecular pharmacology, and high-throughput and high-content screening. Its services support the design and synthesis of biologically active molecules, compound screening, hit identification, lead optimization, analytical characterization, and the development of chemical probes and therapeutic candidates.

Together, these resources provide a strong experimental foundation for translating AI-generated hypotheses, molecular designs, and predictive models into testable chemical and biological discoveries. The successful candidate will be well positioned to develop integrated computational-experimental programs and pursue collaborative research across the College of Pharmacy, the AI (X) Hub, and the OSUCCC – James.

Performance Objectives

Establish a nationally recognized, independent, and externally funded research program at the intersection of artificial intelligence, drug discovery, and chemical biology. Develop and apply innovative AI and computational methodologies that address significant fundamental or translational challenges in therapeutic discovery. Build interdisciplinary collaborations within the Division of Medicinal Chemistry and Pharmacognosy, the College of Pharmacy, the AI (X) Hub, the OSUCCC – James, and the broader Ohio State research community. Contribute to undergraduate, graduate, and professional education through effective teaching in medicinal chemistry, chemical biology, computational drug discovery, artificial intelligence, or related areas.

Education and Experience Requirements

A Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree in chemistry, chemical biology, biochemistry, biophysics, structural biology, or a closely related field. A strong record of fundamental or applied research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and drug discovery, demonstrated through impactful publications, promise or success in securing extramural funding, and professional recognition. Demonstrated creativity and originality, with the potential to establish new concepts, methodologies, frameworks, or applications in AI-enabled drug discovery. Evidence of the potential to develop an independent, collaborative, and externally funded research program. A commitment to excellence in teaching, mentorship, and service.

Additional Information:

Ohio State provides access to a depth and breadth of opportunities and resources. Starting your first day, Ohio State offers you a comprehensive benefits package.

How to Apply

To be considered, please submit your application electronically via Workday/Interfolio. Application materials must include:

Curriculum vitae, including a complete list of publications. Research statement describing previous accomplishments, future research plans, and potential connections to drug discovery research at Ohio State. Teaching and mentoring statement outlining the applicant’s teaching interests, experience, and approach to training students and researchers. Names and contact information for three professional references, who may be invited to provide letters of recommendation.

Application closes 10/15/2026

The university is an equal opportunity employer, including veterans and disability.

The Department of Pharmacology in the School of Medicine at the University of Virginia invites applications for two open rank tenured/tenure-track faculty positions. We are seeking candidates working at the forefront of drug development, mechanisms of drug action, and novel pharmacological approaches, and who bring these tools to bear on fundamental and exciting questions in biology. Successful candidates will join a highly collaborative faculty and have opportunities to build on departmental strengths in metabolism, chemical biology, immunology, cardiovascular and respiratory physiology, and neuroscience.

Qualifications

Successful applicants will have earned a PhD, MD, or MD/PhD, completed a minimum of three years of postdoctoral training, and demonstrated excellence in research with a strong potential of developing innovative research programs that can attract sustained extramural funding. Tenure status and rank of the position depend on qualifications. For appointment with tenure, candidates should have established a nationally reputable, well-funded research program with a track record of high-impact publications.

Competitive salary, space, and start-up packages will be provided. Along with a collegial and inclusive department (https://pharm.virginia.edu), prospective faculty will have access to state-of-the-art core facilities, a vibrant campus-wide research community, and will draw from an outstanding pool of graduate and MD/PhD students in the interdisciplinary Biomedical Sciences (BIMS) program to support their research program.

The University of Virginia is in Charlottesville, which is located in the eastern foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains in Central Virginia, a region renowned for its natural beauty, history, music, and culinary culture. For more information about UVA and the surrounding area, please visit https://www.virginia.edu/life/charlottesville. UVA assists faculty spouses and partners seeking employment in the Charlottesville area. To learn more please visit https://dualcareer.virginia.edu.

Application reviews will begin November 1, 2026, and the positions will remain open until filled.

Application Instructions

To apply, please go to https://apply.interfolio.com/193470 . For full consideration, applications should include the following:

  • Cover letter
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Detailed statement of research accomplishments and interests (3 page max)
  • Contact information for three references (name, email address, telephone number, mailing address)

For questions about this faculty position, please contact Dr. Michelle Bland, Associate Professor of Pharmacology and Faculty Search Committee Chair at mlb2eg@virginia.edu

Biomedical and Translational Sciences/Weill Institute for Cell and Molecular Biology

The Weill Institute for Cell and Molecular Biology (WICMB) and the Department of Biomedical and Translational Sciences (BTS) at Cornell University in Ithaca, NY invite applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level in the College of Veterinary Medicine (CVM).

We welcome candidates with a PhD or equivalent degree who will develop a research program that uses fundamental insights into cellular and molecular mechanisms to drive therapeutic discovery and development. Successful candidates will have expertise in one or more of cell, structural & molecular biology; in situ structural biology; chemical biology; and biomolecular engineering. Research programs may include the discovery and validation of new disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets, small-molecule and biologic discovery and/or delivery, development of organoid and animal models, and engineering of advanced targeted technologies for therapeutic use including but not limited to (epi)genome editing and protein degradation. The successful candidate is expected to develop a dynamic, externally funded research program; lead a vibrant group with a commitment to mentoring, career development of trainees, and inclusive climate; build collaborative connections across basic science and clinical science departments; and endeavor to establish an arm of the research program that advances the animal health goals of the CVM. The candidate will be expected to teach in the pharmacology and/or physiology focus areas.

The WICMB has a broad focus on cell and molecular biology and serves as a hub for molecular life sciences across the university. The Institute’s culture is highly collaborative and current research areas include cell signaling, cell morphogenesis and patterning, structural biology, mechanobiology, neurobiology, membrane trafficking, lipid metabolism, computational biology and protein networks, cell cycle and DNA damage in diverse biological systems spanning microbes to humans.

The BTS department conducts cutting-edge molecular & translational research and innovative teaching & mentoring to advance education and discovery in veterinary and human biomedicine in a collaborative scientific community. Current areas of research strength span cell, molecular, and structural biology; genetics & genomics; cancer biology; developmental biology; and reproductive sciences. The department has a history of leadership in the life sciences and in university-wide research initiatives, including partnerships with Weill Cornell Medicine (WCM).

Life sciences research at Cornell is supported by state-of-the-art facilities, including those for computational biology, genomics, epigenomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, microscopy/imaging, histology, flow cytometry, transgenic mouse models, patient-derived xenograft models, and non-traditional animal models. Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Exercise Medicine Research

Job Description

Virginia Tech seeks to recruit an innovative researcher in the area of exercise medicine with a focus on the impact of exercise/physical activity on health, including but not limited exercise immunology related to cancer prevention, cardiometabolic, skeletomuscular and neurocognitive health for a tenure track faculty position at the assistant professor level. The successful candidate should address issues of the health effects of regular exercise during development in childhood and/or throughout the adult lifespan with a focus on the cellular, molecular and organ systems’ effects of exercise. Investigators who focus on mechanistic understanding of the effects of exercise in human subjects and/or laboratory animal models with innovative genetic, biochemical and/or physiological approaches in addition to strong computational/data analytic skills are encouraged to apply. The person hired for this position will join 44 other faculty led teams at the research institute that currently have an active portfolio of over $240 million in extramural research and training grants and contracts and will join the new FBRI Center for Exercise Medicine Research (CEMR). The position will be located at the FBRI at VTC (https://research.vtc.vt.edu) on the university’s health sciences campus in Roanoke, Virginia. In addition to the original 100,000 square foot research institute that opened in 2010, an adjacent 139,000 square foot additional research building (http://fralinbiomed.info/buildingtour) recently opened in which the new faculty member will have their research program. The new CEMR is immediately adjacent to the research laboratories of the FBRI Center for Vascular and Heart Research, Cancer Research, Addiction Recovery Research Center, Center for Health Behaviors Research, Center for Neurobiology Research as well as Center for Human Neuroscience Research, offering additional opportunities for collaborations that span metabolism, cardiovascular science, cancer and neuroscience research. Facilities at the research institute include multiple research MRIs for human and animal research, including high field MR guided PET and MR guided focused ultrasound, multiple cellular/molecular imaging facilities, including spinning disc confocal microscopy, standard laser scanning confocal microscopy, scanning block face electron microscopy, super resolution microscopy, biochemical and molecular biology cores, including Mass Spec and proteomics as well as behavioral testing suites for animals and humans, as well as two human whole room calorimeters, metabolic kitchen and dining areas for the study of human nutrition and eating behaviors.


Applications will be reviewed continuously until the position is filled. It is expected that initial interviews will begin in October 15th, 2026. The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) Intramural Research Program (IRP) in the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is recruiting a tenure-track/tenure-eligible Investigator on the NIH main campus in Bethesda, Maryland.

NIAMS IRP seeks to identify a tenure-track/tenure-eligible Investigator to develop a vigorous, independent basic science research program within the NIAMS IRP. Applicants must have a Ph.D., M.D., M.D./Ph.D., or equivalent doctoral degree in a relevant field with extensive postdoctoral experience, as well as a strong publication record demonstrating outstanding potential for independent creative research. The ideal candidate should have expertise in basic, translational, computational and artificial intelligence, and/or population research with relevance to key NIAMS mission areas of arthritis, musculoskeletal, and skin biology and diseases. The hired investigator will be expected to develop an exciting independent research program. The successful candidate will benefit from the highly collaborative environment of the NIH IRP.

The successful candidate will have access to state-of-the-art core research facilities and will be assigned generous independent resources to include laboratory support personnel, equipment, space, and an allocated annual budget for services, supplies, and salaries sufficient to foster success.

Salary will be commensurate with research experience and accomplishments. A full Civil Service package of benefits (including retirement, health insurance, paid leave, career support, work-life and commuter benefits, and optional life and long-term care insurance) is available. Relocation Expenses will be offered based on eligibility. All employees of the Federal Government are subject to conflict-of-interest statutes and regulations, including the Standards of Ethical Conduct. Additional information regarding NIAMS is available at: https://www.niams.nih.gov/

Applicants should submit a cover letter (two page maximum), research statement (4 pages excluding references), mentoring statement (1 page), curriculum vitae with complete bibliography, and complete contact information of three references. Questions should be directed to Dr. Markus Hafner at markus.hafner@nih.gov, noting NIAMS Investigator in subject line. Applications should be submitted to Viviana Harrington at viviana.harrington@nih.gov. Applications will be accepted through October 31, 2026 for first-round review. If no selection is made, applications received after this deadline will be considered in subsequent review rounds until the position is filled.

Appointees may be a US citizen, Legal Permanent Resident or non-US citizen who are eligible for a valid work authorization. This position is subject to a background investigation.

DHHS and NIH are equal opportunity employers. Visit https://eeo.nih.gov/ for more information on NIH Equal Employment Opportunity.

description:
The Biological and Environmental Science and Engineering (BESE) Division at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) is seeking outstanding individuals and change-makers to build ambitious research programs that will push the boundaries of technology and advance the goals of global water security. Among several targeted faculty hires, we are inviting applications from high-caliber candidates for open-rank positions (i.e., Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor) who will bring new insights, tangible solutions and renewed focus to the areas of water security, desalination, and sustainable water systems. The BESE Division welcomes applications from all qualified candidates and particularly encourages applications from Saudi nationals and women in the field.

Initial priority areas include, but are not limited to:

  1. Seawater reverse osmosis process optimization
  2. Next-generation membrane and separation technology
  3. Energy-efficient desalination
  4. Brine management, zero-liquid discharge and alternative-source production
  5. Resource recovery and waste valorization
  6. Water system modeling

We seek candidates with clear plans for research translation, including collaboration with in-Kingdom and international partners, and a pathway to validate and implement outcomes in real-world contexts. Successful candidates will be expected to establish and sustain a globally visible, externally competitive research program, position KAUST as a global leader in water security, and contribute to graduate teaching, mentoring, and the training of the next generation of scientists and engineers.

About KAUST

KAUST is a mission-driven graduate research university dedicated to advancing science and technology through interdisciplinary research, education, and innovation. KAUST works closely with national and international partners across academia, industry, and government to translate research into innovative technologies and solutions that support the Kingdom’s strategic priorities, drive economic development, and deliver tangible societal impact.

Located on the shores of the Red Sea in Saudi Arabia, KAUST attracts top faculty, scientists, engineers and students from around the world. Faculty benefit from state-of-the-art research facilities, guaranteed baseline research funding, generous infrastructure support, entrepreneurship opportunities, internationally competitive salaries, and a uniquely international campus community designed to enable both professional excellence and family well-being.

Ranked #1 in the Arab world in the Times Higher Education Arab University Rankings 2026, KAUST is internationally recognized for its research excellence.

Application Instructions

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until positions are filled. Successful candidates will be expected to commence their appointments at KAUST in 2027.

Interested applicants should submit the following materials:

  • A cover letter, including the rank sought and alignment with the priority area(s)
  • A 2-3 page curriculum vitae, including links to your Google Scholar and Scopus profiles
  • A 2-3 page research statement describing a 5-year vision and startup plan
  • A 2-page teaching/mentoring statement
  • A one-paragraph summary of each of your top five publications, describing your contribution, the novelty of the work, and its impact
  • Contact information for 3-5 referees who are acknowledged experts in the field from academia, industry, or other relevant sectors

Recruitment is conducted in accordance with KAUST hiring practices and will emphasize transparent, equitable, and internationally benchmarked evaluation.

For more information about KAUST, please visit http://www.kaust.edu.sa. More information about the BESE Division is available at https://bese.kaust.edu.sa/.

For questions regarding this position or the application process, please contact BESE.jobs@kaust.edu.sa.

description:
O'Donnell Brain Institute Scholars Program

The Peter O'Donnell Jr. Brain Institute (OBI) at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center invites applications to the OBI Scholars Program for exceptional early career scientists of any discipline whose research includes mechanistic studies relevant to human nervous system disease. The program is open to PhD, MD, or MD/PhD applicants seeking their first tenure-track assistant professor position or currently serving as Assistant Professors or recently promoted Associate Professors.

OBI Scholars will receive a generous ~$3M recruitment package and laboratory space in the recently opened, state-of-the-art O'Donnell Biomedical Research Building, which houses a diverse set of investigators, including basic and human neuroscientists, immunologists, biochemists, and structural biologists. The program supports individuals pursuing either laboratory-based or human subject research.

All primary faculty recruited by OBI enter through this single OBI Scholars process. Within OBI, recruitment is guided by several scientific priorities, and a major one is the Program for Memory Longevity (PML), a signature program of OBI in hippocampal circuit biology and memory, led by Attila Losonczy, MD, PhD. PML sits within OBI, and candidates with an interest in PML apply through this same process.

Areas of Recruitment Exceptional applicants from any discipline will be considered. We are particularly focused on three key areas: (1) circuit biology relevant to movement, memory/cognition, and pain; (2) molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration and regeneration, including neuroimmune and endolysosomal mechanisms; and (3) theoretical and computational neuroscience, including models, algorithms, or theory that probe mechanisms of neural circuit function across levels of biological organization. Within these priorities, research may explore fundamental aspects of neuron or CNS function or broadly relevant disease mechanisms, without requiring direct use of disease models.

Resources and Environment OBI Scholars will also have access to:

Advanced imaging and data analysis resources, including two-photon and light-sheet microscopy, STED, spatial transcriptomics (Xenium and Merscope), cryo-EM, and high-performance computing

Human neuroscience infrastructure, including academic neurosurgeons providing access to human brain recordings and tissue, magnetoencephalography (MEG), high-density EEG, and focused ultrasound for blood-brain barrier modulation and lesioning

Extensive cross-campus collaboration, spanning more than a dozen departments and centers, including Neuroscience, Neurology, Neurosurgery, Psychiatry, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, and the Center for Alzheimer's and Neurodegenerative Diseases

OBI programs supporting high-risk/high-reward neuroscience (Visionary Neuroscience Program), trainee development (Sprouts Program, Neural Scientist Training Program, Travel Grant Program), multidisciplinary Research Interest Groups, and clinical research career development (Clinical Neuroscience Research Excellence Initiative) OBI Scholars receive a primary appointment within OBI and a secondary appointment in the basic science or clinical department most aligned with their work. Candidates whose career includes clinical care must have or be eligible for a Texas Medical License.

UT Southwestern ranks among the top academic medical centers in the world, with 4 Nobel Laureates, 3 Lasker awardees, 28 National Academy of Sciences members, and 26 National Academy of Medicine members on faculty.

Qualifications Candidates must hold a PhD, MD, or MD/PhD in neuroscience, immunology, engineering, computer science, biology, physics, or a related discipline, and be seeking a first tenure-track assistant professor position or currently serving as Assistant Professor or recently promoted Associate Professor. A record of research excellence at each level of training and a compelling vision for future work are essential.

All candidates, including those interested in PML, please submit:

  • Curriculum Vitae Cover letter describing your research area and future goals
  • Two-page summary of research accomplishments and future direction (independent investigators should highlight lab discoveries and secured funding)
  • Three letters of recommendation​​​​​
